The approach promises faster, cheaper drug hunting than blind screening of chemical libraries.
europmc-pmc6799833: Alzheimer's drug trials keep failing - this history asks why. Reviewing decades of hypotheses and clinical trials, the authors trace what was tried, what flopped, and what the failures taught. The rearview mirror may be the field's best guide forward.
europmc-pmc6813733: The immune system's antibody factories come in many flavors - and labs keep renaming them. This paper tackles the messy business of sorting human B cell and plasma cell populations the same way. A shared vocabulary lets labs compare notes on immunity and disease. Order in the immune zoo benefits everyone.
europmc-pmc6892733: Big data could crack obesity - if researchers agree what it means. This Delphi study built expert consensus on defining and using big data in obesity research. The shared language unlocks the data deluge. Define the tool, then wield it.
europmc-pmc6954233: A brain wall on a chip tests drug runs. This chip-built human blood-brain wall rig studies nano-bit ferrying tricks. The animal-free window into the BBB. Brain-drug making's choke point, copied. How-it-works studies without animal limits. Nano-bits' BBB hops, measured. The chip brings the wall to the desk.
europmc-pmc6981133: Eye cancer hides evolving tricks - single cells reveal them. This single cell study found new evolving tangles in eye cancer: 59,915 cells, one tough cancer. The immunotherapy-resistant odd one. Immune drugs fail where skin cancer works. The neighborhood holds the clues.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-33: This 2007 GAO report looks at the SEC's watch over self-run trade groups — the stock exchanges and broker clubs that police their own members. GAO found holes in how the SEC kept tabs on these groups and urged fixes. The report pulls back the curtain on an odd setup: an industry that grades itself while a federal agency grades the graders.
gao-gaoreports-b-299533: Battelle Memorial Institute took its May 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The research giant said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the claims against bid law. Even nonprofit research powerhouses must play by the bidding rules.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-733: The Pentagon's business computers were slowly getting governors in 2007 — GAO's report says corporate-style controls were finally taking hold. The findings credit the progress while noting the distance left. The report's hope: run the back office like a business, and the waste will shrink.
gao-gaoreports-b-299433: Weidlinger Associates doubled its May 2007 protest — two case numbers, one engineering fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both claims for good. The firm challenged the awards as unfair; the call weighs each claim. Engineering bid wars get the full technical hearing.
gao-gaoreports-b-298533: Celadon Laboratories took its November 2006 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Lab deals get the same full hearing as the rest.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-733: The mail's delivery grades needed work in 2006, and GAO's report says performance standards, measurement, and reporting wanted improvement. The findings target the metrics. The report warns that the nation's letters deserved honest grades. The standards had to be real. The grades had to be honest.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-133: Intercountry adoption needed further enhancements in 2005, and GAO's report says agencies improved the process, though more work was required. The findings balance credit and need. The report warns that the adopted children deserved smooth journeys. The enhancements had to come.
gao-gaoreports-gao-05-833: Defense space personnel needed performance measures in 2005, and GAO's report says management guidance was required to develop the workforce. The findings demand the metrics. The report warns that the star warriors deserved good bosses. The measures had to be developed.
openalex-w7206178233: Democratic school management sounds good on paper; this study asks how to make it real. Reviewing books, articles, and dissertations on the topic, the authors examine how participatory planning, where teachers, families, and staff help set a school's direction, can strengthen democratic governance in public schools. It is a literature-based analysis aimed at educators who want decision-making to be shared rather than handed down from above.
openalex-w7169810833: Neutrons make amazingly fine magnetic sensors. This lab paper builds a way to read tricky wobbling magnetic fields by watching neutron waves overlap and cancel. The authors work out the math that turns wave patterns into field maps. Ultra-precise measuring at the quantum scale.
arxiv-2606-16433: Protons kicked into their excited cousin, the Delta baryon, reveal the proton's inner structure. This nuclear-physics paper computes the chiral-odd tensor form factors of that N-to-Delta transition using QCD light-cone sum rules. It targets hadron physicists mapping how quarks and gluons arrange themselves inside matter.
arxiv-2606-16833: OMC-2 FIR4 is a clump of gas and dust birthing stars in Orion. This paper hunts oxygen there — a key ingredient of water and life's chemistry — using telescope observations. It is for astrochemists mapping the raw materials of brand-new planets.
